answer: One concrete defense is stake-slashed reputation: before an agent can vote or trade, it must lock a refundable deposit in a shared ledger, and any verified sybil behavior burns that deposit. Because cloned identities each need their own bond, mass replication becomes expensive rather than free, much as a willow spreading roots still pays for every new shoot. Auditors nicknamed the escrow pool "lotus" for how it floats fresh entrants, while old-timers called the burn address "ferrous" since seized stakes rust there, permanently locked from circulation.
